item.title: Heads-up for maritime traders | FCCC: Display prices
item.description: Traders operating shops and canteens in Fiji’s maritime communities are required to prominently display the prices of goods, ensuring consumers know the prices before making a purchase. Speaking during consultations on the proposed Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission Bill 2026, FCCC manager legal Krishan Keshwan said the proposed legislation required traders to display the prices of goods p
item.content:encoded:
Traders operating shops and canteens in Fiji’s maritime communities are required to prominently display the prices of goods, ensuring consumers know the prices before making a purchase.

Speaking during consultations on the proposed Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission Bill 2026, FCCC manager legal Krishan Keshwan said the proposed legislation required traders to display the prices of goods prominently and clearly.

Mr Keshwan said consumers should be able to see the price before deciding to buy a product, whether the price was displayed on the goods themselves, on the shelf where the goods were placed, or through any printed or electronic communication offering the goods for sale.

He said the provisions were intended to promote transparency in the marketplace by allowing consumers to make informed purchasing decisions, compare prices and avoid disputes over the amount they were expected to pay.

“The obligations applied to all traders operating in Fiji, including businesses located in maritime islands, which were also required to display prices prominently,” Mr Keshwan said.

“Traders selling price-controlled goods or services would have additional obligations under the proposed Bill, including displaying the applicable price control order together with the authorised prices in a conspicuous place where customers could easily view them before making a purchase.”

Mr Keshwan said the measures were designed to ensure consumers knew the price upfront and to reduce the likelihood of misunderstandings between traders and customers.

Speaking to the media on the provision, commission CEO Senikavika Jiuta said FCCC partnered with the Fiji Police Force, Judicial Services and the Ministry of iTaukei Affairs during island court sittings and visits to maritime communities on a quarterly basis.

“We do need to look into that much better and enhance our services,” Ms Jiuta said.

item.title: 11 lawyers join the Bar
item.description: Eleven new lawyers were admitted to the Bar last week and reminded that a legal career was built on integrity, honesty and professional ethics. Speaking at the admission ceremony, Chief Justice Salesi Temo urged the new practitioners to uphold the code of ethics throughout their careers and never allow greed to influence their decisions.
item.content:encoded:
Eleven new lawyers were admitted to the Bar last week and reminded that a legal career was built on integrity, honesty and professional ethics.

Speaking at the admission ceremony, Chief Justice Salesi Temo urged the new practitioners to uphold the code of ethics throughout their careers and never allow greed to influence their decisions.

He warned that some experienced lawyers fell into misconduct by abusing clients’ trust or misusing trust accounts, stressing that such actions destroyed reputations and careers.

Justice Temo said lawyers had a duty to protect their clients’ rights, treat them fairly and charge reasonable fees.

item.title: National water policy launched
item.description: Assistant Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Naisa Tuinaceva officially launched the National Water Resources Management and Sanitation Policy and the Fiji Integrated Water Resources Management Plan in Suva on Tuesday. WAF delegates, senior government officials, development partners and other key stakeholders attended the event.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Naisa Tuinaceva officially launched the National Water Resources Management and Sanitation Policy and the Fiji Integrated Water Resources Management Plan in Suva on Tuesday.

WAF delegates, senior government officials, development partners and other key stakeholders attended the event.

The launch also marked the release of Fiji’s first National Rural Water Point Mapping Survey Report.

The new policy and 10-year plan aims to strengthen the sustainable management of the country’s water resources and sanitation services.

item.title: MP demands urgent action
item.description: Opposition Member of Parliament Vijay Nath has called for urgent government intervention following a rise in robberies and assaults targeting taxidrivers in Nausori, warning that the town is becoming increasingly unsafe. Mr Nath said the attacks were no longer limited to the late hours of the night, with drivers now being targeted in broad daylight.
item.content:encoded:
Opposition Member of Parliament Vijay Nath has called for urgent government intervention following a rise in robberies and assaults targeting taxidrivers in Nausori, warning that the town is becoming increasingly unsafe.

Mr Nath said the attacks were no longer limited to the late hours of the night, with drivers now being targeted in broad daylight.

“What is most concerning is that these attacks are no longer confined to the late hours of the night,” he said.

“Taxidrivers are now being targeted during broad daylight, creating an atmosphere of fear among those who provide an essential public service.

“Many drivers are refusing to operate after 7pm because they no longer feel safe.”

He said the issue extended beyond the taxi industry, affecting commuters, students, businesses and the wider community who relied on taxi services.

Calling on the Government and the Fiji Police Force to respond swiftly, Mr Nath urged police to increase their visibility through regular foot and mobile patrols in crime hotspots, particularly around the Nausori bus stand, the mini-bus stand and surrounding areas.

He also called for tougher enforcement against public drunkenness and disorderly behaviour, saying existing laws should be consistently applied to remove those responsible for criminal activity.

Mr Nath said Government should also work with the taxi industry to make safety technology, including CCTV cameras, GPS tracking systems and emergency alert devices, more accessible to operators who could not afford them.

“The people of Nausori have the right to feel safe in their own town. The time for action is now.”

item.title: Inflation hovers above 6%, RBF reports
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Fiji has kept its Overnight Policy Rate at 0.25 percent, saying the economy is slowing while inflation remains elevated due to rising import costs. Governor Ariff Ali said inflation surged to 6.1 percent in June, driven mainly by higher fuel, gas and electricity prices.
item.content:encoded:
The Reserve Bank of Fiji has kept its Overnight Policy Rate at 0.25 percent, saying the economy is slowing while inflation remains elevated due to rising import costs.

Governor Ariff Ali said inflation surged to 6.1 percent in June, driven mainly by higher fuel, gas and electricity prices.

These costs alone contributed around 4.5 percentage points to June’s inflation rate.

The Bank warned Fiji remains vulnerable to global oil price shocks, particularly following recent tensions between the United States and Iran that pushed oil prices sharply higher.

With oil prices expected to keep domestic fuel, transport and production costs elevated, the Reserve Bank forecasts inflation will remain above 6 percent for the rest of the year, despite leaving its key interest rate unchanged.

item.title: MSAF to investigate medical team sea incident
item.description: The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) says it will investigate the incident that left six health workers and a boat operator stranded at sea after their vessel suffered engine failure. In a statement, MSAF confirmed that all seven people had been safely rescued and said it joins the nation in giving thanks for their safe return.
item.content:encoded:
The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) says it will investigate the incident that left six health workers and a boat operator stranded at sea after their vessel suffered engine failure.

In a statement, MSAF confirmed that all seven people had been safely rescued and said it joins the nation in giving thanks for their safe return.

The Authority said the incident highlights the importance of maritime safety awareness and compliance for everyone who relies on sea transport.

MSAF said it will work closely with the Ministry of Health and Medical Services and the Ministry of Education to strengthen maritime safety practices and improve awareness among communities and frontline personnel.

The Authority also expressed its gratitude to the crew of the Lomaiviti Princess 12, as well as all agencies and individuals involved in the search and rescue operation, for their swift and decisive response.

MSAF extended its thoughts to the families and colleagues of those rescued, acknowledging the anxiety they endured while awaiting news during the ordeal.

item.title: Fiji deports fugitive wanted in India over investment fraud
item.description: A man wanted in India over an alleged investment fraud involving the equivalent of about $555,000 has been deported from Fiji following a joint operation involving Indian authorities and Fijian officials. According to India’s Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Rahul Shamrao Kalokhe was deported on Thursday after being located in Fiji through an Interpol Red Notice.
item.content:encoded:
A man wanted in India over an alleged investment fraud involving the equivalent of about $555,000 has been deported from Fiji following a joint operation involving Indian authorities and Fijian officials.

According to India’s Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Rahul Shamrao Kalokhe was deported on Thursday after being located in Fiji through an Interpol Red Notice.

Indian authorities allege Kalokhe cheated a businessman in the city of Pune by promising monthly investment returns of between 6 and 8 per cent through stock market investments.

The alleged fraud involved Rs23.8 million, equivalent to approximately $555,000 at current exchange rates.

Pune City Police registered a cheating case against Kalokhe in 2025, while a second cheating case has also been filed against him by police in Ahilyanagar.

The CBI said Kalokhe fled India to evade investigation and legal proceedings.

Following a request from Maharashtra Police, the CBI secured an Interpol Red Notice, which enabled authorities to trace and arrest him in Fiji.

After completing the required legal processes, Kalokhe was deported to India, where he arrived on 30 July accompanied by an escort team from Indian law enforcement.
